title: Control-Theoretic Stability Analysis of RLHF Training Dynamics

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong causal chain: RLHF instability is a real deployment risk. Identifying stability regimes and connecting them to control-theoretic predictions would directly inform safer training procedures. The phase portrait approach makes the theoretical prediction concrete and testable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running RLHF training requires significant infrastructure (reward model training, PPO loop, KL tracking). Beginners would need substantial mentor support to set up the RLHF pipeline even on a simple task. Control theory background adds conceptual overhead. Medium compute may be sufficient but the engineering complexity is high.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple moving parts: train a reward model, run RLHF with noisy rewards, track KL divergence per step, plot phase portraits, compare against control-theoretic predictions. Each component is a substantial sub-project. Unlikely to complete cleanly in 30 hours.
